governing_intent: Build the smallest canonical-Python substrate that can actually reach the provisioned SWF-08 sandbox — installation-token acquisition and refresh, live repository and Projects v2 read, fenced one-way projection write, resident authenticated webhook ingress, sandbox profile composition and live `doctor` transport probes — and prove it independently and locally-repeatably, so that PY-10 enters its single coherent live proof with transport defects already removed from the failure surface.
summary: The SWF-34 amendment landed cleanly and closed the isolation defect that produced the previous NEEDS_CLARIFICATION. Binding rule 6 (docs/work-units/python/PY-09B.md:38-42), scope item 8 (:54) and acceptance criterion 10 (:90-93) now separate a permission-enforced repository boundary from a configuration-enforced Project boundary, explicitly forbid claiming token-level Project isolation, and name PY-10 AC 16 as the compensating control — matching docs/decisions/2026-09-21-sandbox-isolation-standard.md exactly and matching the residual risk recorded at docs/operations/py10-sandbox.md:62-86. The second gap from that assessment is also closed: verification requirements now state that the independent verifier executes the bounded live portion itself on the provisioned host (:101). The stale 'Open prerequisite: a Founder scope decision' paragraph in PY-10.md is gone, replaced by the SWF-33-resolved text at PY-10.md:147-152. The premise of the BIU remains factually correct against clean main 30d0703: github_work_management.py:16 takes `snapshot` and `projection_write` as injected callables with no HTTP path; github_webhook.py:99 binds 127.0.0.1:0 inside a test-helper contextmanager; installation/domain/github_profile.py:13-21 carries no App identity, installation id, bind address or port; composition/doctor_probes.py covers only Git worktrees and the worker executable; pyproject.toml declares no runtime dependency. Intent, non-goals, twelve acceptance criteria and the offline/bounded-live/proven-red iteration surface SWF-33 demanded are all bounded and observable, and the requirement links are honest about extent ('the first **live** GitHub adapter behind the existing port'). One new owner-level defect of the same class SWF-34 named as its durable lesson now blocks release, and it was masked by the isolation question last time. Scope item 2 and AC 3 require 'the Git-level access candidate custody requires against the sandbox repository', exercised live. Candidate custody in the accepted tree is a real push and a fresh clone: real_worker.py:70 calls `publish_and_read_back`, which pushes to the configured remote (git_source_control.py:57) and then `ls-remote` + `clone --no-checkout` (git_source_control.py:41-49); docs/evidence/candidate-publication-invariant.md makes publication a precondition of accepting RESULT=VERIFY. The sandbox repository is **private** (docs/operations/py10-sandbox.md:13), and binding rule 4 — marked not delegated — fixes the installation grant at exactly `issues: read`, `metadata: read`, `organization_projects: write`, with AC 2 requiring that a simulated extra grant fail the check. A GitHub App installation token with no `contents` permission cannot clone a private repository and cannot push to any repository. AC 3 is therefore unsatisfiable under the permission set the same contract pins, and the word `contents` appears nowhere in PY-09B.md, PY-10.md or the sandbox provisioning record. The provisioning preflight never exercised it — its repository checks are 'issues readable' and 'installation scope excludes production' (docs/operations/py10-sandbox.md:98-101), never a clone or a push. AC 9 inherits the same wall: the accepted `doctor` source-control check requires `'contents:write' in publication_permissions` plus a 40-character baseline read back (installation/application/doctor.py:165), so an honest live probe against this installation must FAIL, and supplying the permission from an adapter-declared mapping is exactly the 'passing on an adapter-declared flag alone' that AC 9 forbids. Everything else an implementer faces is research inside constraints that already exist.
owner_clarifications: The sandbox App installation grants no `contents` permission, and PY-09B requires live Git candidate custody against a private repository. Binding rule 4 (not delegated) fixes the grant at exactly `issues: read`, `metadata: read`, `organization_projects: write`; AC 2 requires a simulated extra grant to fail the check; the preflight at ~/.local/share/alienintent-bootstrap/py10_preflight.py enforces that same exact set as 17/17. Scope item 2 and AC 3 require the Git access candidate custody needs to be exercised live against `AlienLogicLab/alienintent-sandbox`, which docs/operations/py10-sandbox.md:13 records as private; the accepted custody path pushes a candidate branch and clones it back (real_worker.py:70, git_source_control.py:41-57), and docs/evidence/candidate-publication-invariant.md makes that publication a precondition of VERIFY. An installation token without `contents: read` cannot clone a private repository and without `contents: write` cannot push to any repository. AC 9 compounds it: doctor.py:165 requires `contents:write` in the read-back publication permissions for the source-control probe to pass. An implementation agent cannot add an App permission (App configuration is browser-only and Founder-owned, and the installation must re-accept it) and cannot weaken a non-delegated rule. The Founder must either (a) grant `contents: write` to the sandbox App installation, restate binding rule 4 / AC 2 / the operations record and the preflight to the four-permission set, and record why write rather than read is the least privilege custody actually needs; or (b) remove live Git custody from PY-09B scope item 2 and AC 3 and state where that capability is owned instead — noting that PY-10 AC 12 ('exact candidate custody is proven before every VERIFY') and AC 15 ('doctor passes against the sandbox') hit the identical wall, so deferring it recreates exactly the unowned-capability defect SWF-33 was created to fix. Making the sandbox repository public would enable anonymous clone but still not push, so it does not resolve (a).
implementation_unknowns: How to mint the App JWT. pyproject.toml declares no runtime dependency and the stdlib has no RS256 signing, so the choice between a first adapter-layer dependency (PyJWT/cryptography, which the bootstrap preflight already uses) and shelling out to openssl is ordinary engineering. The fitness vendor-signature check bans vendor types only in domain/ports signatures, so either is permitted at the adapter boundary.

The shape of the live GitHub client behind the existing ports: REST for app/installation/token/repository/issues, GraphQL for Projects v2 field and option identities, inside the PY-05 port contracts and the hexagonal adapter rules that already constrain it.

How the fence is realized. Projects v2 offers no compare-and-set on `updateProjectV2ItemFieldValue`, so 'carries the expected revision and refuses on conflict' must be canonical-side fencing plus read-back — which is what FD-01 requires and what github_work_management.py:59-75 already demonstrates against its own revision map.

How to originate a real signed delivery repeatably for AC 7. With `issues: read` the App cannot self-trigger an `issue_comment`; the one App-writable trigger is the Project field update from scope item 4, which emits the subscribed `projects_v2_item`. Whether GitHub redelivers an installation's own Project writes to that installation needs empirical confirmation, with a manual trigger as fallback.

Extending GitHubProfile with App identity, installation id, private-key reference, ingress bind address and port while keeping doctor's `_configuration` check (doctor.py:117-125) meaningful, and how the profile factory locates ~/.config/alienintent-sandbox/profile.json without embedding installation detail in source — composition is the only layer the fitness `configuration` check permits to read the environment.

How the resident ingress is started and stopped for the bounded live checks without entering PY-10 territory. The CLI has no resident mode: `serve_webhook` (github_webhook.py:86-107) is a test-helper contextmanager on an ephemeral port, and FactoryCoordinator.start() is a synchronous drain. The smallest sufficient answer under SWF-20 is a bounded harness-owned server lifetime bound to the profile's configured host and port, not a new long-running command.

How the live portion is kept out of the default collected suite (markers or an env-gated skip) so AC 12 holds on a runner with no sandbox credentials. .github/workflows/python-architecture-fitness.yml runs `pip install pytest` then `pytest -q` with no project install and no credentials, and tests/ currently contains no skip/marker gating convention to copy.

Where the redacted evidence is retained. The contract names no path; the repository convention is docs/evidence/ (PY-01, PY-06, PY-07 precedents) rather than the docs/verification/ that PY-10 mandates for its report, and docs/verification/ does not exist.

A stable non-reversible way to prove 'the run used the sandbox identity' (AC 11) without emitting App ID, installation ID or hostname — for example a salted digest of the identifiers compared against the profile.
verification_assessment: Real executable proof rather than description, and better sequenced than any prior BIU in this cohort. Every capability in scope carries a named negative control — invalid or missing credential reference, simulated extra and missing grant, stale projection write, unsigned/wrong-signature/replayed delivery, fail-closed Project identity resolution, a failing case for each doctor probe — and AC 5, AC 7, AC 9 and AC 10b go further by requiring proven-red demonstration (remove the fence, use the wrong secret, deny an adapter-declared pass) in line with SWF-24. The offline/bounded-live split is stated rather than assumed, which is precisely what SWF-33 demanded, and the verification-first repair sequencing clause is satisfiable here because the fixture-backed harness can exist before any live call. Two gaps from the previous assessment are now closed: AC 10 no longer asserts the unprovable token-level Project isolation, and line 101 now binds the independent verifier to executing the bounded live portion itself on the provisioned host against the same sandbox identities. Three weaknesses remain. First and decisive, AC 3 and the passing half of AC 9's source-control probe cannot be satisfied by the permission set binding rule 4 pins, so a verifier reading them literally must reject a candidate that is behaving correctly — the same failure shape SWF-34 removed from AC 10, one criterion over. Second, AC 12's 'the Python suite passes' collides with CI, which installs only pytest on a hosted runner with no credentials and no project install, so the live/offline boundary must be mechanized and any new dependency must reach the workflow. Third, AC 11's redaction obligation is in tension with AC 7's requirement to prove the delivery arrived through the provisioned endpoint and with AC 10b's requirement that evidence name the exact Project targeted; the scheme must not destroy the isolation proof it protects, and must not be read as licence to redact docs/operations/py10-sandbox.md, which legitimately publishes those identifiers and is not source, tests, logs, diagnostics or retained evidence.
material_risks: AC 3 as written is unsatisfiable against the provisioned installation, and binding rule 4 is marked not delegated. The predictable outcome is a candidate that implements token acquisition, Project read, fenced projection and ingress correctly, documents honestly that Git custody is impossible without a `contents` grant, and is rejected at VERIFY for failing a criterion it could not satisfy — an entire repair cycle spent on a decision only the Founder can make.

The same missing grant blocks PY-10 AC 12 and AC 15, so resolving it by narrowing PY-09B's wording alone would push a first-of-kind live capability into the capstone with no owner — exactly the decomposition defect SWF-33 was created to fix.

Widening GitHubProfile ripples through doctor's `_configuration` check, both composition roots (composition/github_profile.py, composition/offline_profile.py) and the existing profile tests, so a defect in the profile shape is the one failure mode in this BIU that is not module-local.

Introducing the repository's first runtime dependency requires a matching change to .github/workflows/python-architecture-fitness.yml, which installs only pytest and never installs the project — unnamed work that SWF-20 makes a mechanically detectable verification finding unless treated as lifecycle-necessary for AC 12.

AC 7 depends on GitHub redelivering an event the installation itself caused. If it does not, the only repeatable in-band trigger disappears (the App cannot comment with `issues: read`) and the 'bounded, repeatable, individually diagnosable' property SWF-33 required degrades toward a manual one-shot — which also weakens the verifier's ability to execute the live portion independently as line 101 now requires.

Binding rule 3 forbids App ID, installation ID and hostname in source, tests, logs, diagnostics and evidence, while docs/operations/py10-sandbox.md commits exactly those values; an implementer or verifier could read the rule as requiring that operations record be redacted, which is out of scope and would destroy the environment documentation PY-10 depends on.

Scope item 5's 'resident' ingress has no home in the current CLI, and the boundary between a bounded harness-owned server and a new long-running service sits directly against the non-goal 'this BIU does not run the factory loop' — the cheapest correct answer risks reading as under-delivery, the fuller one as scope expansion.
SWF-09 applies: the invocation path used for the live checks may report neither token nor monetary cost, which must be recorded UNKNOWN and never assumed zero.
next_action: Put the single permission question to the Founder: grant `contents: write` to the `alienintent-py-10-sandbox` App installation (163346526), re-accept the installation, update the preflight and docs/operations/py10-sandbox.md to the four-permission least-privilege set, and amend PY-09B binding rule 4 and AC 2 to match — or, alternatively, remove live Git custody from scope item 2 and AC 3 and name where PY-10 AC 12 and AC 15 get that capability instead. In the same pass, decide whether the retained redacted evidence lands in docs/evidence/ (repository convention) or docs/verification/ (PY-10's mandate). Then reassess PY-09B against the amended contract and release it through normal SWF-21 admission; nothing else in the contract is holding it back.
rationale: SWF-34 did what it was asked to do. Rule 6, scope item 8 and AC 10 now describe a property GitHub can actually enforce, the residual organization-wide Projects grant is named as accepted risk with PY-10 AC 16 as its compensating control, the verifier's live-execution obligation is explicit, and the stale PY-10 paragraph is cleared. The decision inputs behind this BIU are all closed — SWF-08 provisioned and verified the target, SWF-09 fixes budget policy, FD-01 fixes projection direction, FD-02 through FD-06 and the Architecture Authority constrain the implementation, PY-05, PY-06, PY-08 and PY-09 are accepted and on main — so almost everything an implementer faces is research inside existing constraints: which JWT library, which GraphQL queries, how to gate live tests, how to bound the ingress lifetime. None of that is owner work and none of it should be treated as such. There is still no case for splitting: outbound API access and inbound ingress share one profile, one credential path and one set of doctor probes, and the only repeatable way to originate a real delivery runs through the projection write, so the two halves verify each other rather than standing apart. What stops this being READY is narrow, cheap, and precisely the class of defect SWF-34 recorded as its own durable lesson — an acceptance criterion describing something the platform cannot provide under the permissions the same contract pins as not delegated. Last time it was Project isolation; this time it is Git custody against a private repository with no `contents` grant, which the isolation question masked because both live in the same permission set. The provisioning record's own check list shows it was never exercised: issues were read, the installation scope was confirmed, and no clone or push was ever attempted. An implementation agent that hits this must either weaken a rule it is forbidden to weaken, fabricate a permission in adapter-declared evidence that AC 9 explicitly forbids, or fail a criterion it cannot satisfy. That is owner work, and a single permission grant plus a matching one-line amendment converts an unsatisfiable criterion into a satisfiable one without touching anything else in the contract.
